Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center. EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: dilg.gov.ph CILG OPiNiON NO. LIO VICE MAYOR SILVANIO C. ZANORIA Municipality of Aurora Province of Zamboanga del Sur Dear VM Zanoria: S. 2048 This has reference to your letter dated 7 June 2017 seeking the Department's legal opinion on the following issues contained in said letter, and we quoted here in verbatirn, to wit: I. S•Vho can declare the position of a Barangay Kagawad, who is absent from sessions and other duties since October 10, 2016 until the present and who is considered a fugitive from justice, vacant? 2. Can the Sangguniang Bayan take action on a complaint against Barangay Officials (Section 61(c) of RA # 7160) even without a verified complaint, in this case only by virtue of resolution duly adopted and passed Sangguniang Barangay (as complainant)? 3. Are Barangay Officials, including other elected officials of the LGU, covered by the Civil Service Code? Since this Department was not given the reason/s why the Sangguniang Barangay Member (Barangay Kagawad) was considered as fugitive from justice, allow us to quote the definition of fugitive from justice given by the Supreme Court in the case of Rodriguez vs. COMELEC, et all, referred to as the "MARQUEZ decision in this manner: "figitive from justice includes not only those who flee after conviction to avoid punishment but likewise those who, afier being charged, flee to avoid prosecution " In DILG Legal Opinion No. 03, S.2016 dated 21 January 2016, this Department has opined that: ' G.R. No. 112889, 18 April 1995

"If such evasion of warrant of arrest and thus, evasion of prosecution of charges is committed during the incumbency of the local elective official, then the relevant provision would already be Section 46(a) of the Local Government Code of 1991, which provides: SECTION 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. - (a) o rnor ci Punorw Barangay is temperarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as. but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor, city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking Sangguniang Barangay member shall automatically exercise thepowers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. Based on the foregoing, the grounds for temporary vacancy in the office are not limited to those enumerated therein, such as leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office. Said provision uses the phrase "such as but not limited to" which only implies other similar cases, like the case herein. Notably, the LGC is bereft of any provision delineating the procedure in filling up of temporary vacancies in the sanggunian, what Section 45(a) Of the LGC delineates is the procedure in the filling up of permanent vacancies in the sanggunian. However, in Menzon vs. Petilla2, the Supreme Court held that the mode of succession provided for permanent vacancies may likewise be observed in case of a temporary vacancy in the same office. Thus, in DILG Legal Opinion No. 19, S.2017 it was settled by this Department that: applying the rule on succession which is the procedure in filling up of subsequent vacancies in the office of' the vice-mayor and in the sanggul?ian. the highest-ranking Sangguniang Bayan Member shall become the Acting VIZe-Mayor. The 21d ranking Sangguniang Bayan Member shall become the 1st-ranking and so forth The resultant vacancy shall be filled-up in accordance with Section 45 of the Local Government Code of 1991'3. G.R. No. 141307, 28 March 2001 J SECTION 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunian. (a) Permanent vacancies in the Sanggunian where automatic successions provided above do not apply shall be filled by appointment in the following manner:

Be that as it may, with respect to the constant absenteeism of the said elective official, please be guided that the Department has settled in its previous legal opinions that an elective official is deemed in the service of their constituents regardless of time and place. Thus, they are given wide latitude of discretion on how to effectively run their respective LGUs. They may not be present at their respective offices but this does not mean that they are automatically absent from work. To bolster this, the Supreme Court in the case of Macatangay vs. Chairman of Commission on Audit/ has ruled that: "In fact, they are not even required to keep a record of their daily attendance such as by accomplishing Civil Service Form NO. 48 (Daily Time Record) or punching the bundy clock. -xxx xxx Elective officials, indeed, are deemed in the service of their constituents regardless of time and place. There can be no occasion to consider them absent from work since their presence at such specified time and place is not a pre-requisite to their collection of salary for services rendered. " Considering that the Sangguniang Barangay Member is considered as fugitive from justice coupled with other circumstances (e.g. his physical absence in the Office of the Sanggunian and his non-performance of duties as Sangguniang Barangay Member) already amounts to a temporary incapacity to perform his duties and functions5. As to your second query, you have informed us of the existence of Barangay Resolution No. 10, S. 2017 of Barangay Bag-ong Pitogo which endorses to the Sangguniang Bayan of Aurora, Zamboanga del Sur, the concern of former against its Sangguniang Barangay Member for continued absenteeism. (b) Except Ibr the Sangguniang Barangay, only the nominee ofthepoliticalparty under which the Sanggunian member concerned had been elected and whose elevation to the position next higher in rank created the last vacancy in the Sanggunian shall be appointed in the manner hereinaboveprovided. The appointee shall come from rhe same political party as that of the Sanggunian member who caused the vacancy and shall serve rhe unexpired term of the vacant office. In the appointinentherein mentioned, d nomination and a certificate of membership of the appointee from the highest official of che political party concerned are conditions sine qua non, and any appointment without such nomination and certification shall be null and void ab initio and shall be a ground for administrative action against the official responsible therefor. (c) In case the permanent vacancy is caused by a Sanggunian member who does not belong to any political party, the local chiefexecutive shall, upon recommendation of the Sanggunian concerned, appointa qualified person to fill the vacancy. xxx xxx G.R. No. L-38728, 30 September 1982 ' DILG Opinion No. 03, S. 2016.2/

May we reiterate our previous legal opinion which stated that a sanggunian resolution is not the proper way of initiating an administrative complaint. Quoted hereunder is the pertinent provision of the said legal opinion: "A reading of the Sangguniang Barangay Resolution would reveal that in view of the unauthorizedabsences of the concerned Barangay Kagawads, the Sangguniang Barangay, through a Resolution, simply recommended to the Sangguniang Bayan their removal. To our mind. this is not the valid complaint, verified or under oath. ontem Iat ec bn 1 sim I an ex ression of sen i Re tion d o inion of' the San n; Faranga_v. Such being the caset for failure to comply with the form prescribed under Section 61 of the Local Government Code, said Resolution cannot validly initiate the administrative complaint against the concerned Sangguniang Barangay Membersø. " Section 61 of the LGC is quoted herein for your perusal and ready reference: "SECTION 61. Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints. - A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows: (a) A complaint against any elective official of a pro vin ce, a highly urbanized city, an independent component city or component city shall be filed before the Ofhce of the President; (b) A complaint against any elective official of a m unicipality shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlalavvigan whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President; and (c) A complaint against any elective Barangay official shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang bayan concerned whose decision shall be final and executory. " As to your third query, appointive officials, including those elected officials of the LGUs are included in the coverage of the Civil Service. Sections 6 and 9 Chapter 2, Subtitle A, Title l, Book V of Executive Order NO. 292, otherwise known as the "Administrative Code of 1987 "will enlighten us on the matter, and quoted herein:

"SECTION 6. Scope of the Civil Service, - (I) The Civil Service embraces all branches, subdivisions, instrumentalities, and agencies Of the Government, including government-owned or controlled corporations with original charters. (2) Positions in the Civil Service shall be classified into career service and non -career service. SECTION 9. Non-Career Service. — The Non-Career Service shall be characterized by (I) entrance on bases other than those of the usual tests of merit and fitness utilized for the career service; and (2) tenure which is limited to a period specified by law, or which is coterminous with that of the appointing authority or subject to his pleasure, or which is limited to the duration of a particular project for which purpose employment was made. The Non -Career Service shall include: (l) Elective officials and their personal or confidential staff; However, in relation to your previous query and as discussed above, the office hours provided for in the Omnibus Rules implementing Book V of EO No. 292 and other pertinent Civil Service Laws cover only appointive officials and employees of the government. Neither does the LGC fix or provide office hours of elective local officials. Fixing their working hours would unnecessarily delimit their services to the prejudice Of their constituents and ultimately, the public service. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter.
